excerpt: Narvar is a San Francisco post-purchase platform for retailers: delivery promises, order tracking, notifications and returns. CEO Anisa Kumar since 2024.
content:
Narvar sells post-purchase software to retailers and brands, covering what happens after a shopper clicks buy. Its products include Promise, which shows AI-powered delivery date estimates at checkout; Track, branded order-tracking pages; Notify, proactive delivery messages; Shield, returns and exchanges management with fraud controls; Secure, for protecting orders; and Assist, an AI assistant for order questions. Its website now describes these as agentic products and pitches intelligent personalisation beyond the purchase.

Narvar was founded in 2012 by Amit Sharma, a retail supply chain veteran who had worked at Apple, Walmart and Williams-Sonoma, Retail TouchPoints reported. TechCrunch covered a $10 million round in 2015 and a $22 million Series B in 2016. In August 2018 Narvar raised a $30 million Series C led by Accel, with Battery Ventures, Salesforce Ventures and Scale Venture Partners, bringing its total to $64 million; FreightWaves and Retail TouchPoints reported that the money would go into products and international growth. In October 2024 Narvar promoted chief customer officer Anisa Kumar, a former Levi's, Walmart and Target executive, to CEO, and Sharma moved to an advisory role, FashionUnited reported.

Narvar does not publish prices; retailers request a demo. It is built for mid-size and large retailers and brands shipping many orders, and competes with post-purchase and returns tools such as parcelLab, Loop Returns and AfterShip.

We have not used Narvar for this page. It brings together Narvar's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
